v.rationale: The three implementations share almost the same core: a FormRequest, a Hash::check credential check, createToken, currentAccessToken()->delete(), and a named limiter keyed on the lowercased email plus IP. All suites pass. Probes showed that only impl-1 returns a JSON 401 to guests who send no Accept header, via redirectGuestsTo in bootstrap/app.php; impl-2 and impl-3 return a 500 ('Route [login] not defined'), a real problem for mobile clients. All three return a 500 for an array-valued email because the limiter reads it before validation. All three correctly return JSON 422/401 without an Accept header, include Retry-After on 429, and resist case and whitespace bypass. impl-1 also has the most thorough tests, so it ranks first. impl-3 is second: its tests are stronger (limit reset after a minute, other token still works) and its controllers use validated() and an invokable /me controller, but it lacks the email rule. impl-2 is third: it passes Stringable objects into the query, hashing and token calls, uses a closure /me route, and has slightly weaker tests.
